evidence.section: Tensile and Creep Rupture Properties and Correlation to Microstructure
evidence.quote: The large decrease in strength of LC at the longest aging condition could be associated with the precipitation of Z -phase noted in the WAXS results.
The LC steel was more resistant to creep than 0Nb except when aged for 10,000 h, where there is evidence of Z -phase formation, and MX depletion, in the LC alloy.
0Nb also showed evidence of δ -ferrite despite phase modeling predicting the onset of δ-ferrite formation at higher temperatures.
Loss in creep strength in 0Nb is likely a function of the aforementioned inclusion of small islands of δ-ferrite.
